post.description: For the break-glass role, in a browser session, after a step-up when auth.stepUp is configured; never on one's own request. The request must be pending approval, or approved and held by its change windows, and still hold the change set (and head) given. It merges through its delivery like any approved request, past its change windows; the platform's own policies still apply. The alert recipients and the owning team are alerted, and a post-incident review opens.
post.summary: Merge a request without its approvals (break-glass)

post.description: For platform admins, auditors and the request's owners, in a browser session, after a step-up when auth.stepUp is configured; never the person who broke glass, the requester or their delegates. Each person signs off once and a sign-off is never withdrawn; the second closes the review.
post.summary: Sign off the post-incident review of a break-glass
Cancel a request

post.description: Says which decision a link of an approval card in chat (Microsoft Teams) opens the request with, for the person signed in. It changes nothing: the decision is confirmed with the review, which checks the link again. A link is refused (403, type https://quai.dev/problems/chat-link-refused) when it was changed, has expired, was sent to someone else, or the request was decided or changed since; the refusal is in the audit log.
post.summary: Check the link of an approval card in chat

get.description: The JSON bundle is the evidence: verify it offline with quai audit verify --bundle and the checkpoints' public key. Its proof, the segments of the audit log up to a signed checkpoint, is for auditors of all repositories and platform admins signed in (docs/design/09-security-and-compliance.md#evidence-bundle). Each download is an audit event.
